sections.heading: Black money and money laundering — concepts and scale

blocks.text: **Black money** is income **concealed from tax or generated illegally** — the stock of unaccounted wealth and the parallel-economy flows that feed it. **Money laundering** is the process of making dirty money look clean, classically in three stages: **placement** (injecting cash into the system — smurfing, shell deposits), **layering** (obscuring the trail — shell companies, round-tripping via tax havens, trade misinvoicing, hawala) and **integration** (return as 'legitimate' assets — real estate, gold, equity). Estimates of India's shadow economy have ranged widely (NIPFP's ~20% of GDP era estimates to higher unofficial claims) — write 'estimates vary; the phenomenon is structural', not a fake-precise number.

rows: Tax evasion (under-reporting by professionals/firms); cash-heavy sectors — **real estate, gold, elections**
**Hawala** (informal value transfer without movement of money)
Corruption and rent-seeking; leakages from public spending
**Shell companies** and layered corporate structures (~3.4 lakh struck off post-2017)
Crime proceeds: narcotics, smuggling, extortion
**Trade-based laundering** — over/under-invoicing of exports & imports
Regulatory arbitrage: capitation fees, black-market premia
**Round-tripping** via tax havens; participatory-note opacity (since tightened); crypto mixers (new frontier)

blocks.text: **Costs**: fiscal loss (tax-GDP ratio suppressed), distorted asset prices (real estate), unfair competition against honest firms, criminal-political financing, and **monetary-policy blur** (cash economy dulls transmission).

items: **PMLA, 2002** (ED enforces): attachment/confiscation of proceeds of crime, reversed burden in some contexts; **Vijay Madanlal Choudhary (2022)** upheld ED's powers (arrest, twin bail conditions) — review pending on aspects; critique: conviction rate very low relative to cases, and alleged selective use — carry both the tool and the concern.

**Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income & Assets) Act, 2015** — steep tax+penalty on offshore concealment; **Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Amendment, 2016** — property in fictitious names confiscable; **Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018** (post-Mallya/Nirav Modi) — property confiscation of absconders.

**Demonetisation (Nov 2016)**: 86% of currency withdrawn; verdict — ~**99.3% of notes returned (RBI)**, so the 'stock' of black cash wasn't destroyed, but digitalisation accelerated and the tax base widened; SC upheld the process 4:1 (2023). Present it as a costly formalisation shock, not a black-money kill-shot.

**Systemic drains**: GST + e-invoicing (transaction trails), **Aadhaar-PAN linkage**, TDS/TCS webs, SFT reporting, cash-transaction limits (₹2 lakh), electoral-bond experiment **struck down (Feb 2024)** for opacity — election finance remains the black-money heartland.

**Global rails**: FATF membership (India rated largely compliant, 2024 mutual evaluation), **Automatic Exchange of Information/CRS**, FATCA, DTAA renegotiations (Mauritius/Singapore capital-gains loophole closed 2016), BEPS/global minimum tax.

blocks.code:
flowchart TD
  A[Dirty money generated] --> B[Placement - cash into system]
  B --> C[Layering - shells, hawala, trade misinvoicing]
  C --> D[Integration - real estate, gold, equity]
  D --> E[Looks legitimate]
  F[Counters: PMLA-ED, Benami Act, FEOA] --> C
  G[Prevention: GST trails, PAN-Aadhaar, AEOI, digital payments] --> B
  H[Frontier: crypto, election finance] --> C

sections.heading: AP angle and the balanced verdict

items: **AP textures**: real-estate cash intensity around capital-region speculation (Amaravati land dealings drew ED/CID attention across regimes); **red-sanders smuggling** (Seshachalam forests) as a crime-proceeds chain; sand mining rents; liquor-trade cash; granite/mineral under-invoicing — each maps a generation channel to a local industry.

**Verdict for mains**: India has moved from **episodic amnesties** (voluntary disclosure schemes) to **architecture** (trails + attachment + exchange of information). The unfinished core: **election finance transparency**, low PMLA convictions, real-estate opacity (a transactions registry with beneficial-ownership disclosure is the next reform), and safeguards against agency misuse — an anti-black-money regime is credible only when it is even-handed.

blocks.text: Exam tip: Define the two terms separately (generation vs cleaning), draw the three-stage laundering flow, then group counters as punitive (PMLA/Benami/FEOA), preventive (GST/PAN/digital) and global (FATF/AEOI). Demonetisation gets two balanced lines with the 99.3% fact. Close on election finance + agency even-handedness.

prelimsPointers: Money-laundering stages: **placement → layering → integration**.
**PMLA 2002** enforced by the **Enforcement Directorate**; Vijay Madanlal Choudhary (2022) upheld core powers.
**Demonetisation (8 Nov 2016)**: ₹500/1000 notes (~86% of currency); **99.3% returned** (RBI Annual Report 2018); upheld by SC (2023, 4:1).
**FEOA 2018**: offences ≥ ₹100 crore; declared fugitives' property confiscable without conviction.
**Benami Amendment 2016**: up to 7 years RI; property vests in the Centre.
**Electoral bonds struck down — ADR v. Union, Feb 2024** (right to information of voters).
**FATF**: global AML/CFT standard-setter; India a member since 2010; 2024 evaluation placed India in 'regular follow-up' (top band).
Cash transaction cap: **₹2 lakh (Sec 269ST, IT Act)**; red-sanders smuggling is the AP-specific illicit-trade example.
mainsAngles: Distinguish black-money generation from money laundering and map India's counter-architecture onto each.
Demonetisation formalised the economy more than it destroyed black wealth — critically assess with evidence.
Election finance is the mother lode of black money — discuss in the light of the electoral-bonds verdict.
Enforcement without conviction breeds both impunity and fear — evaluate the PMLA-ED regime's record and safeguards.
Trace how global cooperation (FATF, AEOI, DTAA reform) closed the offshore routes of Indian black money.

glossary.definition: Processing criminal or concealed income through placement, layering and integration so it appears legitimately earned.
Informal value-transfer system settling claims through trusted broker networks without actual movement of money across borders.
Domestic money sent abroad (often to tax havens) and returned disguised as foreign investment to claim legitimacy or treaty benefits.
Property held in another's name while the consideration flows from the real beneficiary — confiscable under the amended 1988 Act.
Shifting value across borders by misinvoicing trade — over-priced imports or under-priced exports masking transfers.
The natural person who ultimately owns or controls an asset or entity — the disclosure target of modern AML rules.

blocks.text: Growth needs capital: physical (machines, infrastructure), human (health, skills) and financial (savings intermediated into investment). India's **investment rate (GFCF)** slid from **~34% of GDP (2011-12)** to ~27–28%, recovering to ~30–31% led by **public capex** (Union capex tripled to ~₹11 lakh crore budgets); **household savings** remain the base but their **net financial savings dipped to multi-decade lows** (~5% of GDP) as household debt rose — the capital-scarcity problem is thus one of **mobilisation, intermediation and confidence**, not just quantum.

rows: Domestic savings → investment
Falling net financial savings; gold/real-estate preference
Financial inclusion (Jan Dhan ~53 crore accounts), pension/insurance deepening, sovereign gold bonds era, capital-market widening (11+ crore demat accounts)
Private corporate capex
The post-NPA 'wait for demand' decade
Twin-balance-sheet clean-up, PLI, corporate-tax cut (2019: 22%; new mfg 15%), Gati Shakti pipeline
Infrastructure finance
ALM mismatch killed bank-led infra lending
**NIP (₹111 lakh crore)**, **NaBFID**, InvITs/REITs, **National Monetisation Pipeline (₹6 lakh crore)**, municipal bonds
Foreign capital
FDI plateaued (~$70–80 bn gross), FPI volatility
Liberalised FDI (automatic-route dominance), FTAs, GIFT-IFSC, JPMorgan bond-index inclusion (2024) — stable debt flows
Human capital
Public health ~1.9–2%, education ~2.9–3% of GDP vs 2.5%/6% goals
NEP 2020, Ayushman Bharat, skilling missions — the slowest-moving gap

sections.heading: Lack of inclusive growth and sustainability — the twin qualifiers

items: **Inclusion deficit**: growth concentrated by region (south-west vs east), sector (services enclave) and class — **top 1% income share ~22%** (World Inequality Lab estimates); female LFPR low though rising; informal employment ~90%. Yet **MPI poverty fell steeply** — NITI/UNDP estimate **~13.5 crore exited multidimensional poverty (2015-16 → 2019-21)**; extreme-poverty counts now very low on World Bank recalibrations — the honest picture: **poverty falling, inequality high, jobs the missing middle link**.

**Sustainability deficit**: growth's resource intensity — 14 of the world's 20 most polluted cities; groundwater over-draft (Punjab-style paddy economics), land degradation ~30%, climate exposure (heatwaves, cyclones on AP's own coast). Commitments: **Net Zero 2070; 50% non-fossil capacity by 2030 (achieved ahead of schedule in capacity terms), 45% emission-intensity cut**; instruments — PAT, carbon-market rollout, green hydrogen mission, RE ~200+ GW.

**Why they belong with 'insufficient capital'**: exclusion wastes human capital; unsustainability destroys natural capital — growth accounting that ignores both overstates true (inclusive, green) wealth: the **Green GDP / natural-capital accounting** argument.

**Framework close**: the challenge triad — capital, inclusion, sustainability — resolves into one sentence: India must **raise investment while broadening its beneficiaries and decoupling it from carbon** — the operational meaning of 'Viksit Bharat 2047'.

items: **Capital**: AP's high debt limits state capex — hence the hunt for external assistance (World Bank/ADB Amaravati funding revived 2024), PPP ports, and central capex-loan windows (Special Assistance to States).

**Inclusion**: AP scores strongly on delivery (DBT saturation, PDS, Aarogyasri) and poverty reduction, but shows the model's limits — welfare-heavy budgets vs capex squeeze; regional gaps (north-coastal AP & Rayalaseema vs coastal core) mirror the national spatial-inequality problem inside one state.

**Sustainability**: AP is a renewable leader (solar parks — Kurnool among the world's largest; wind ~9 GW; pumped-storage pipeline on the Eastern Ghats seams) and simultaneously cyclone-exposed — adaptation (shelters, mangroves, early warning) is its second sustainability agenda.

blocks.text: Exam tip: Treat this as the thesis note for the whole paper: growth's three qualifiers (capital, inclusion, sustainability). The five-gap capital table + the poverty-vs-inequality honest picture + Net Zero anchors serve essays and interviews alike. Always end with the one-sentence synthesis.

prelimsPointers: **GFCF** ~30–31% of GDP recently, from ~34% (2011-12); Union budget capex ~₹11 lakh crore scale.
Corporate tax cut (Sept 2019): **22%** existing, **15%** new manufacturing companies.
**NIP**: ₹111 lakh crore (2020–25); **NMP**: ₹6 lakh crore asset monetisation; **NaBFID (2021)** — infra DFI.
**MPI**: ~13.5 crore Indians exited multidimensional poverty between 2015-16 and 2019-21 (NITI Aayog).
Climate pledges (updated NDC): **Net Zero by 2070**, 50% non-fossil installed capacity & 45% emission-intensity reduction by 2030.
India's **50% non-fossil power capacity** milestone was reached in 2025 — ahead of the 2030 target.
**Kurnool (Orvakal) ultra-mega solar park** in AP is among the world's largest single-location solar facilities.
Household **net financial savings** fell to ~5% of GDP (2022-23) — a flagged macro concern.
mainsAngles: India's constraint is no longer ideas but investable capital — examine the savings-investment slide and the public-capex bridge strategy.
Poverty is falling while inequality stays high — reconcile the evidence and derive the policy priorities.
Growth that liquidates natural capital is statistical, not real — argue for sustainability-adjusted growth accounting.
Can welfare saturation and capital expenditure coexist in a state budget? Analyse with Andhra Pradesh's trade-off.
Outline the capital, inclusion and sustainability conditions for 'Viksit Bharat 2047'.

glossary.definition: Investment in physical assets (construction, machinery, IP) — the economy's capacity-building expenditure; the investment rate is GFCF/GDP.
Public investment stimulating (not displacing) private investment by creating demand, infrastructure and confidence.
Growth whose processes and outcomes broadly benefit all sections — employment-intensive, regionally spread, poverty-reducing.
Deprivation-based poverty measure across health, education and living standards (10–12 indicators) — beyond income lines.
The stock of environmental assets (water, soil, forests, clean air) whose depletion conventional GDP ignores.
Leasing operating public assets (roads, stations, transmission) to private players for upfront value while retaining ownership.

blocks.text: AP's budget (recent budgets in the **₹2.9–3.3 lakh crore** range) is financed from four streams: **(1) State's Own Tax Revenue (SOTR)** — SGST (largest), state excise on liquor, stamps & registration, sales tax/VAT on petroleum, motor-vehicle tax; **(2) own non-tax revenue** — mining royalties, forestry, interest; **(3) central transfers** — the state's share in the divisible pool (**tax devolution: AP's inter-se share ~4.05% per the 15th FC**) plus grants (revenue-deficit grants, centrally sponsored schemes); **(4) borrowings** — market loans within the FRBM net-borrowing ceiling. The structural feature to memorise: **AP is a revenue-deficit state** — it borrows partly to fund current expenditure, not only capex.

rows: **Bifurcation wound**
Lost Hyderabad — ~**45% of undivided AP's revenue** came from the capital region; AP kept ~58% population with a farm-heavy base
The founding fiscal grievance; basis of Special Category Status demand
**Revenue deficit persistence**
Committed expenditure (salaries, pensions, interest) + large DBT welfare absorb revenue receipts
15th FC gave AP among the larger **revenue-deficit grants** (~₹30,000+ crore over the award)
**High debt**
Outstanding liabilities around **one-third of GSDP** (with off-budget borrowings via corporations/guarantees flagged by **CAG** additionally)
Interest payments eat a large slice of revenue; FRBM ceilings bind capex
**Narrow own-revenue base**
No metropolitan services/IT hub of Hyderabad's scale; SOTR/GSDP moderate; liquor-policy swings destabilised excise
GST compensation ended (June 2022) removing a cushion
**Vertical dependence**
Central transfers ~40%+ of receipts in many years — exposure to FC formulas & CSS matching burdens
Cess/surcharge growth shrinks the divisible pool AP shares

items: **Revenue side**: GST compliance drives (e-invoicing, analytics), excise-policy recalibration, stamps/registration buoyancy via capital-region activity, mining-royalty rationalisation, monetisation of land banks — each carries volatility or one-off character; the durable fix is **GSDP growth that widens the SGST base**.

**Expenditure side**: DBT rationalisation and beneficiary deduplication, pension reform debates (GPS/OPS oscillation), subsidy targeting (power dues to DISCOMs are the hidden deficit), and protecting capex from being the residual casualty.

**Borrowing side**: staying within net-borrowing ceilings (Centre now nets off off-budget borrowings after 2022 tightening), lengthening maturities, external assistance (World Bank/ADB for Amaravati, KfW/JICA lines) — cheaper but project-tied.

**Federal claims**: revenue-deficit grants, bifurcation-related dues (covered fully in the next note), and the **16th FC** representation — AP's case rests on low per-capita income relative to peers and the bifurcation shock.

**Evaluation**: AP's fiscal strategy shows the classic welfare-state dilemma in miniature — high social transfers with a narrow base produce **debt-financed welfare**; sustainable only if growth (ports, corridors, aqua, energy) outruns interest costs. A balanced answer credits delivery efficiency while flagging the CAG's off-budget and guarantee cautions.

items: Numbers to carry (bands, honestly): budget size ~₹3 lakh crore; devolution share **4.047% (15th FC)**; debt ~33–35% of GSDP (plus guarantees); revenue deficit persistent since 2014; central transfers ~40% of receipts.

Standard structure: four resource streams → five constraints table → three-sided coping (revenue/expenditure/borrowing) → federal claims → balanced verdict. Update the current-year figures from the latest AP budget speech and CAG State Finances report before the exam.

blocks.text: Exam tip: The examiner wants the STRUCTURE of AP's fiscal stress (bifurcation base-loss → revenue deficit → debt-financed welfare → capex squeeze), not a recital of scheme names. The 45%-revenue-from-Hyderabad fact is the single most powerful line in any AP-finance answer.

prelimsPointers: AP's inter-se share in central tax devolution: **4.047% (15th Finance Commission)**.
Undivided AP drew roughly **45% of its revenue from the Hyderabad region** — the bifurcation fiscal shock.
AP has needed **revenue-deficit grants** under the 15th FC — a marker of structural imbalance.
**GST compensation** to states ended **June 2022**; compensation cess continues only to repay COVID-era loans.
Major SOTR heads: **SGST > state excise > stamps & registration > fuel VAT > motor-vehicle tax** (order varies by year).
Since 2022 the Centre **nets off off-budget borrowings** against states' borrowing ceilings; CAG has flagged AP's corporation borrowings/guarantees.
**FRBM** net borrowing ceiling for states: ~3% of GSDP (+0.5% power-reform incentive when applicable).
mainsAngles: Anatomise Andhra Pradesh's budgetary resources and explain why the state remains in revenue deficit a decade after bifurcation.
Debt-financed welfare is AP's fiscal signature — evaluate its sustainability and the reforms that could square the circle.
Losing Hyderabad was a fiscal amputation — assess the bifurcation's continuing impact on AP's resource base.
How do central transfers shape AP's budget, and what should the state argue before the 16th Finance Commission?
Off-budget borrowings hide the true deficit — discuss with the CAG's observations on state finances.

glossary.definition: Taxes a state levies and collects itself — SGST, excise, stamps, vehicle and fuel taxes — the measure of fiscal self-reliance.
Excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts — borrowing to pay for current consumption rather than assets.
Obligations that cannot be pruned in the short run — salaries, pensions and interest — which pre-empt fiscal space.
Debt raised by state corporations/SPVs serviced from the budget but historically outside deficit numbers — now netted against ceilings.
Finance Commission grant (Art 275) to states whose assessed revenue needs exceed capacity after devolution.
State's contingent liabilities backing corporation loans — invisible until invoked, hence the CAG's disclosure insistence.
